watch_next: The chair said engineering quotes would come back for a vote in January if the numbers are available.
The 23 Cove Road owner is to be placed on the first January meeting agenda, and the Hickory Hills well discharge is to go on a future agenda.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to approve a notice of intent for a warehouse distribution facility on one of the town's roads, with a standard order of conditions.
It approved a single-family home at 680 Reservoir Road and a septic replacement at 45 Perimeter Road, each with standard conditions.
A request to remove trees at 411 Goodrich Street ended in a negative determination, with conditions on debris, stump grinding and replanting native hardwoods.
Four other filings, at 400 Leominster Shirley Road and three on one road, were continued to December 7th.
A new part-time conservation administrator was announced to start November 28th; the commission met without one.

why_it_matters: Wetlands approvals set the conditions on new building near protected land in town, and the commission is currently running without a conservation administrator until the new part-time hire starts.

The commission also reported on revolving and trust funds and a maintenance need at Hollis Road, which draw on money outside the tax-supported budget, and a driveway repair at Howard Street has no funding source identified yet.
watch_next: December 7th: the commission takes up the four continued filings.
November 28th: the new part-time conservation administrator starts.

meetings.headline: Conservation Commission issued negative determinations for four requests and continued three round road hearings; no administrator.
meetings.summary: Held by Zoom with no conservation administrator. The commission acted on several requests for determination, continued three Round Road retaining wall notices of intent and a warehouse notice of intent to November 16th, and heard a contested enforcement matter at 23 Cove Road that was referred back for review. It also approved a purchase order for bridge repairs and took up other routine business.

what_happened.line: The commission voted negative determinations on four requests: paving at Chase Road, tree cutting at White Street, and driveway paving at Townsend Harbor Road.
The commission continued three Round Road retaining wall notices of intent and the Falulah Road warehouse notice of intent to November 16th.
The 23 Cove Road enforcement order was referred to an outside person for review; no enforcement will proceed until an administrator is hired.
The commission approved a larger purchase order for bridge repair materials after the existing one proved much smaller than thought.
The meeting ran by Zoom with no conservation administrator, and the commission voted no interest in acquiring a Sunny Hill Road parcel.

why_it_matters: With no administrator, enforcement matters such as the Cove Road order are on hold, so property owners and neighbors face a delay in resolution until a hire is made.
The Round Road wall and Falulah Road warehouse projects stay open until the November 16th hearing, which is when abutters can next raise concerns about drainage and wall placement.
watch_next: Conservation Commission meeting on November 16th: continued Round Road and Falulah Road warehouse hearings.
Whether an administrator is hired, which the commission said must happen before any Cove Road enforcement proceeds.
